title: What is an AI front desk?
description: An AI front desk is a customer-facing assistant that answers routine questions, captures context, and helps visitors take the next step.
intro: The useful comparison is not AI versus people. It is an always-available first response layer that knows its approved information and knows when a person should take over.

articleSections.heading: It answers from business knowledge
articleSections.body: A useful AI front desk should work from the information the business has reviewed: services, pricing, locations, policies, and other approved sources. When that knowledge is missing, the system should say so or escalate.

articleSections.heading: It helps a visitor decide what to do next
articleSections.body: The outcome is not only an answer. It may be a lead, a booking click, an enrollment request, a callback, or a human conversation with context attached.

articleSections.heading: It gives the team a feedback loop
articleSections.body: Questions, handoffs, and incomplete flows show where the website or workflow needs improvement. That makes the front desk a learning surface for the business.

title: AI front desk vs. live chat: what is the difference?
description: Compare AI front desks and live chat across coverage, response time, knowledge, handoff, and team ownership.
intro: Live chat and an AI front desk can work together. The key difference is who handles the first response, how the answer is grounded, and what happens when a person needs to join.

articleSections.heading: Coverage
articleSections.body: Live chat depends on a person being available. An AI front desk can handle routine questions around the clock and surface the conversations that need human attention.

articleSections.heading: Knowledge and consistency
articleSections.body: Live staff bring judgment and nuance. An AI front desk brings consistent answers from the approved knowledge base and an explicit fallback when that knowledge is insufficient.

articleSections.heading: Handoff is the bridge
articleSections.body: The choice does not have to be either-or. A strong workflow answers what it can, captures context, and gives a human the thread when the customer needs judgment.

title: Why website visitors leave without contacting your business
description: Find the common gaps between a visitor's question and the next step your business wants them to take.
intro: Visitors do not always leave because they are not interested. They may be unsure about fit, pricing, location, timing, trust, or what happens after they submit a form.

articleSections.heading: The answer is hard to find
articleSections.body: If services, hours, locations, policies, or pricing are scattered across pages, a visitor has to do the navigation work alone. A front desk can bring the relevant information into the conversation.

articleSections.heading: The next step is unclear
articleSections.body: A page can explain the service and still leave the visitor wondering whether to call, book, request an estimate, or ask a question. Make the action explicit and contextual.

articleSections.heading: The form asks for too much or too little
articleSections.body: A blank form creates work for the visitor and the team. A conversational flow can ask a few useful questions, keep the intent attached, and stop when it has enough context.

articleSections.heading: Nobody is available after hours
articleSections.body: Visitors who arrive outside business hours need a safe, honest next step. Capture their request and set a clear follow-up expectation instead of leaving them at a dead end.

title: Form vs. conversational lead capture: when to use each
description: Choose between a traditional form and conversational intake based on the complexity of the visitor's decision and the context your team needs.
intro: Forms are efficient when the visitor knows what they want and the fields are stable. Conversation helps when the visitor needs guidance or the right fields depend on the first answer.

articleSections.heading: Use a form when the request is clear
articleSections.body: A form can be the fastest path for a known request with a short, predictable set of fields such as a quote request or a simple callback.

articleSections.heading: Use conversation when fit matters
articleSections.body: If the visitor needs help choosing a service, location, class, or appointment type, asking one useful question at a time can reduce confusion and improve context.

articleSections.heading: Use a hybrid when you need both
articleSections.body: A conversational flow can answer questions and then display a compact form for the final required fields. The visitor gets guidance without losing the efficiency of structured capture.

title: How to add an AI assistant to a website
description: A practical path from website content to an AI assistant you can review, test, install, and improve.
intro: Adding a widget is the easy part. The durable implementation is the knowledge, workflow, handoff, and measurement around it.

articleSections.heading: Start with the website and source of truth
articleSections.body: Identify the pages, documents, services, policies, locations, and booking paths the assistant should use. Remove or correct information that should not be repeated.

articleSections.heading: Define what the assistant can do
articleSections.body: Choose the actions that matter: lead capture, booking, enrollment, callback requests, notifications, or CRM delivery. Keep each action narrow enough to test.

articleSections.heading: Set the handoff boundary
articleSections.body: Decide when the assistant must ask for a person, when it should fall back, and what context staff should receive. This matters even more for regulated or safety-sensitive businesses.

articleSections.heading: Test before publishing
articleSections.body: Ask real customer questions, check citations or source context, review missing answers, and verify the completion path. Then install the widget and monitor the first conversations.

title: AI front desk readiness checker for your website
description: Score the content and conversion signals that make a website ready for an AI front desk, then see the next improvement to make.
intro: This quick self-assessment is a starting point, not a crawl report. Answer four questions about your site to get a practical readiness score and a next step you can act on today.

sections.heading: What a ready website usually has
sections.body: An AI front desk can only be as useful as the business information and next steps it is allowed to use. Clear source material makes review, testing, and handoff safer.
bullets: Services and locations are easy to find
Hours, policies, and contact details are current
The booking or inquiry path is clear

title: A website AI front desk with clear control boundaries
description: Keep business knowledge, lead data, integrations, retention, and human handoff visible and reviewable as you add AI to your website.
intro: Trust comes from knowing what the assistant can access, what it can do, when it must stop, and how your team can inspect the result.

sections.heading: Tenant-scoped business knowledge
sections.body: Business workspaces keep their sources, conversations, leads, actions, and analytics separated. The assistant works from the knowledge and configuration connected to that business.

sections.heading: Controlled actions and integrations
sections.body: Owners decide which actions are enabled and which integrations can receive a completion. Provider secrets stay in the server-side connection path, not in the public widget.

sections.heading: Privacy and human control
sections.body: Configure lead consent, privacy notices, retention settings, fallback behavior, and human handoff so the experience matches how your business wants to operate.

title: Build a more useful first response for every customer
description: FrontDeskWise is building the operating layer between a local business website and the people who need an answer.
intro: The product starts with a simple belief: a website should do more than publish information. It should help a visitor understand, decide, and take the next step while keeping the business in control.

sections.heading: A product principle: URL → answer → lead → booking
sections.body: Every feature is evaluated against that loop. Knowledge matters because the answer needs to be right. Actions matter because the conversation should lead somewhere. Analytics matter because the team needs to improve the system.

sections.heading: Built for teams that already have a way of working
sections.body: FrontDeskWise is designed to connect to the business's existing website, CRM, booking, email, webhook, and team workflows instead of asking every business to start over.
